label: GO step after an unrewarded visit to S2, when the agent picks a1 (model-based switch toward S1)
explanation: Fires only at GO steps, and only when the D1 reward input was 0 (never after a reward, never at D1 or D2). Among those steps it fires when the previous trial reached S2 and the policy now favours a1, i.e. the model-based move of heading for S1 after S2 paid nothing. Every activation whose previous state is known has prev_state == 2 (the prev_action x prev_common counts match exactly). prev_state != 1 also lets in the window-first trial, where prev_state is unknown in the data but the GRU did see it. Magnitude grows with the a1 policy logit: 52% of mass is in the top choice bin, and coverage by activation quartile is 0.69 / 0.86 / 0.90 / 0.99. About 7% of mass is weak firing when the policy leans a2. It does not fire after rewarded trials, after S1 was reached, or when a2 is strongly preferred. Precision is about 0.69: many matching steps stay silent (often repeated unrewarded S2 visits), which keeps this at partially explained. No future variables: model_act is the agent's own policy at GO. With action == 1 in place of model_act the scores are nearly the same.
